content: Colleges are continuing to verify applications and process admissions, while students have been advised to complete fee payment promptly to ensure a smooth start to the academic session

content: A delegation of the AP Aided Junior Colleges Part-Time Lecturers’ Association submits a memorandum to the YSRCP president outlining a range of concerns related to pay, job security and regularisation

content: Parliament disruptions continue over Amit Shah’s ‘absence’; Congress leader K.C. Venugopal protests outside  Parliament building

title: Andhra Ministers take anti-drug outreach to ASR district’s remote Paderu hamlet
content: Home Minister V. Anitha and Tribal Welfare Minister Gummadi Sandhya Rani visited Sappiputtu in Paderu mandal, distributed saplings and seeds of alternative crops, and said the government was working towards zero ganja cultivation in the tribal belt

content: University urges local bodies, farmers and the public to adopt coordinated control measures as monsoon accelerates breeding of invasive pest

title: Amaravati Pickleball League begins in Vijayawada
content: The government is keen on transforming the State into ‘Healthy Andhra Pradesh’ by promoting sports and physical fitness among people, says Sports Minister

content: Pema Khandu says concerns raised by a community-based organisation in the Taksing area of Upper Subansiri district need to be heard and verified on the ground

title: Akhil Marar severs ties with Twenty20, levels allegations against party chief Sabu M. Jacob
content: Actor-director Akhil Marar has cut ties with the political party Twenty20, alleging that its president, Sabu M. Jacob, failed to honor commitments regarding his candidacy in the 2026 Kerala Assembly elections.

title: Indian government does not endorse comments made at Sheikh Hasina press meet, says MEA
content: The government has no role to play in what was an event by a private media entity, says MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal

title: Kerala HC gives State govt. two weeks to inform long-term measures taken after Kalladi debris slip
content: Court asks State to report on establishing a monitoring cell to oversee environmental clearance granted for construction activities, process for consulting area residents before a project is launched, and re-evaluation of project reports pending for more than three years

content: The structure appeared to lean towards one side, while police personnel kept onlookers away from the building

content: A Bench of Justices M.M. Sundresh and P.B. Varale said it was not inclined to examine Sai’s plea since the Gujarat government had agreed to an expeditious hearing of the pending appeal

title: USFDA, DCA discuss ways to boost pharma manufacturing and drug quality in Andhra Pradesh
content: Andhra Pradesh’s massive pharmaceutical manufacturing base is crucial for supplying medicines to U.S.A., says Country Director of USFDA India Office

title: 16 Maoists, with six carrying ₹39 lakh bounty, surrender before Jharkhand Police
content: “The surrender of Santosh Mahto, a regional committee member of the banned CPI (Maoist), was one of the big achievements for the Jharkhand Police”

title: 'Avoid Lutyens web': PM Modi's advice to 45 NDA MPs at breakfast meet
content: In the meeting, which also included the rebel factions from the Uddhav Sena and Mamata Banerjee's TMC, PM Modi said: "No one should say anything trashy on TV. Maintain full dignity at all times. Engage actively in social media through Facebook, Instagram and X; interact with youth, inform government welfare work, encourage youth for sports activities." Modi advised the MPs to follow the party line and calmly present their views on every issue.

title: Hasina-linked exiled cricketer ready to face murder trial, seeks safe return
content: The 39-year-old has not retired from international cricket and said he still hopes to play one final series for Bangladesh at home before representing the country at the 2027 ODI World Cup.

title: 'We demand that NTA be dissolved': CJP on CBI charge sheet in NEET 2026 case
content: The CBI has filed a chargesheet in the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak case. This investigation implicates several NTA-appointed subject experts in a multi-state conspiracy. Leaked questions were allegedly circulated through intermediaries for financial gain. The Cockroach Janta Party demands the NTA's dissolution and conversion into a new commission. They also seek a thorough probe into all recent paper leaks across India.

title: Michael Dell's son Zach Dell wants his Base Power batteries in every American backyard
content: Zach Dell's company Base Power is expanding its home battery business across America.  The company offers a unique membership model, replacing high upfront costs.  Base Power recently secured one billion dollars in new funding, valuing it at thirteen billion.  This expansion includes plans for international markets like the United Kingdom and Germany.  The firm is also increasing its battery manufacturing capacity to meet growing demand.

title: 'He's like me, but better': McCullum's verdict on England's new Test coach Fleming
content: Brendon McCullum endorses Joe Root's reinstatement as the England Test captain, emphasizing that Harry Brook's chance to lead will come naturally in time. McCullum mentioned that England remains committed to nurturing Brook's leadership abilities. Additionally, Stephen Fleming has taken over as the head coach for the red-ball team and is regarded as an exceptional choice to follow McCullum's lead.

title: Education, jobs, inflation: CJP launches petition asking PM Modi to address India's youth
content: The Cockroach Janta Party has initiated an online petition directed at Prime Minister Modi, urging him to tackle pressing youth issues in education and job creation. Highlighting unemployment as a critical national challenge, the party celebrated the recent resignation of the Union Education Minister. With an aim for nationwide growth, the CJP is gearing up for grassroots mobilization to address these concerns.

title: Priscilla Chan founded a school in 2016; 10 yrs later, it closed after $125m funding
content: After ten years of service, The Primary School, co-founded by Priscilla Chan, will conclude its operations in June. This institution, known for offering tuition-free education and extensive family support, struggled to achieve state-average academic results despite receiving generous funding from the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative. The Initiative has decided to redirect its philanthropic priorities towards funding scientific research instead.

title: Islamic Nato taking shape? What Saudi-Pak-Turkey Mecca pact means for Iran & Israel
content: Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, and Turkey signed a new defence pact in Mecca. This agreement commits them to mutual defence against any armed attack. The deal combines Saudi financial power, Turkish defence industry, and Pakistan's military strength. It comes amid regional tensions involving Iran, Israel, and the United States. This pact signals a shift towards regional security architecture development.

title: Mushroom that causes 'tiny people' visions traced to one species
content: A groundbreaking discovery reveals that a unique mushroom species, Lanmaoa asiatica, is linked to vivid hallucinations involving tiny figures experienced by communities far and wide. Despite lacking known psychoactive substances upon chemical examination, researchers suspect an unidentified compound is responsible for these captivating visual effects. Unraveling this mystery could provide profound insights into perception and the nature of human consciousness.

title: After 420 rejections, Indian woman lands New York job but keeps balance
content: After enduring a staggering 420 rejections, an Indian woman triumphantly landed her first job in New York. She highlights that while her career is essential, it doesn’t define her identity. This refreshing viewpoint contests the traditional notion that work should take precedence over personal fulfillment. With plans to prioritize her well-being alongside her demanding role, she inspires others to adopt a more balanced professional outlook.

title: Elon Musk's preferred state halts data center approvals; says 'prove' this
content: Texas Governor Greg Abbott has ordered a temporary halt to new data center approvals.  Regulators must complete a comprehensive audit before projects can move forward.  Developers must prove electricity and water use, and tax incentives.  Abbott stated Texans must come first in all state decisions.  This move addresses growing scrutiny over rapid data center expansion.

title: Will you have to pay to use UPI? 7 FAQs on possible MDR & what it means for consumers
content: The government is expected to permit a Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) of between 0.25% and 0.4% on UPI transactions above Rs 2,000 made to businesses, while person-to-person payments are likely to remain outside the scope of the proposed levy. The proposal is not expected to affect routine purchases such as milk, vegetables, groceries or payments for auto-rickshaw and taxi services.

title: 'Get Harshit Rana and Rinku Singh': Ashwin names MI's ideal Hardik Pandya trade
content: Speculation surrounds Hardik Pandya's future with the Mumbai Indians franchise.  Ravichandran Ashwin discussed potential IPL trade scenarios involving other teams.  He suggested Kolkata Knight Riders could be a strong contender for Pandya.  Ashwin believes Mumbai must receive significant player value in any deal.  The Mumbai Indians are considering rival team strengthening in trade discussions.

title: Food for thought: Global food prices rise in July as cereals, sugar turn costly
content: In July, global food prices saw a notable rise, with cereals, vegetable oils, and sugar reflecting increased costs. Wheat and maize surged due to weather conditions and market apprehensions. Vegetable oils peaked since June 2022, bolstered by robust demand. Sugar prices also rebounded, driven by weather impacts and expectations around ethanol use. Conversely, meat and dairy prices faced a downturn during this period.

title: Roman Reigns vs. Brock Lesnar net worth in 2026: WWE salaries, earnings & more
content: Roman Reigns and Brock Lesnar have contributed to the modern era of WWE. Mostly, with blockbuster rivalries, championship reigns and record-breaking paydays. Reigns is currently the highest-paid on WWE’s active payroll, but Lesnar has made his fortune through WWE, UFC, and premium appearances. An all-out comparison of their projected net worth, career earnings, endorsements, business ventures, investments and future earning potential for 2026.

title: Revisiting Jannik Sinner And Anna Kalinskaya romance as past relationship resurfaces
content: Jannik Sinner proved himself once again by winning the Wimbledon championship in 2026. He demonstrated his continuing prowess in tennis. Maintaining a low profile, he has been dating Danish model Laila Hasanovic after parting ways with accomplished Russian tennis player Anna Kalinskaya in 2025. Sinner’s focus on his professional growth is evident as he navigates his personal and athletic life.

title: Coco Gauff’s inspiring story: How family belief fueled her Grand Slam glory
content: Coco Gauff’s rise to Grand Slam success is also the story of her family’s belief. Her parents changed their lives to support her dream, stayed by her side through pressure and celebrated every milestone with her. From Wimbledon at 15 to the 2023 US Open title, Gauff’s journey shows how faith, sacrifice and family can shape a champion.

title: Amitabh Bachchan reveals why he has worn tinted glasses for 25 years as he ages
content: On the sets of Kaun Banega Crorepati, Amitabh Bachchan shared a heartfelt explanation behind his signature tinted glasses, noting that they adeptly hide the signs of aging around his eyes. His emotional admission was accompanied by an apology for delays attributed to technical adjustments. The legendary actor is currently enjoying the success of his latest project, Kalki 2898 AD. Read on to know more.

title: 'US itself regulates foreign funds': MEA hits back at American lawmaker's FCRA Bill remark
content: Ministry of external affairs rejected criticism of its foreign funding law.  The ministry stated that legislative matters are internal decisions for Parliament.  Several countries, including the United States, also regulate foreign financing.  A US Congressman criticized proposed amendments to India's Foreign Contribution Regulation Act.  He warned these changes could affect India-US bilateral relations.

title: Rain fury grips Delhi-NCR: Waterlogging cripples commute amid IMD's red alert
content: Delhi and NCR experienced heavy rainfall on Friday morning. Waterlogging affected several areas, including Safdarjung Hospital and the airport. Traffic movement was significantly disrupted across the city and its surroundings. The India Meteorological Department recorded substantial rainfall amounts in various locations. Light rainfall is expected to continue over Delhi for the next two days.

title: Sri Lanka announces free stadium entry for fans in India Test series
content: The two-match series begins on August 15 in Galle. The first Test will be played at the Galle International Stadium, while the second match is scheduled at the SSC in Colombo from August 23 to 27.

title: 'Exercise restraint, act according to law': US urges Pakistan amid PoK crackdown
content: The United States has called on Pakistan to show restraint amidst escalating protests and violence. Officials emphasized the importance of creating conditions that foster free and fair elections while ensuring information access. Protests in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir concerning refugee representation have resulted in numerous casualties. Additionally, voting in seven constituencies has been delayed due to security issues, with the government countering casualty estimates as inflated.

title: 'Why fear eggs in politics?' SC tells Mauha freedom fighter took bullets to chest
content: A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu said it was not inclined to interfere with the high court's direction requiring the Krishnanagar MP to join the investigation. Senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan, appearing for Moitra, argued that she should be allowed to appear before the investigating officer virtually as she was entitled to do so under the law.

title: Saudi Arabia, Pakistan & Turkey sign 'Mecca' pact for mutual defence; India reacts
content: The agreement was signed following a joint defence summit attended by Saudi crown prince Mohammed bin Salman, Turkish president Recep Tayyip Erdogan and Pakistani prime minister Shehbaz Sharif, who attended after performing the Umrah pilgrimage in the city. According to Pakistan's foreign ministry, the pact is "guided by the longstanding historical ties among the three states, based on the enduring bonds of brotherhood.

title: Watch: Locals use makeshift raft to ferry schoolkids through flooded Delhi streets
content: Heavy rain lashed Delhi, inundating low-lying areas and disrupting traffic significantly. Residents in Valmiki Basti waded through waist-deep water, facing decades of recurring flooding. The Municipal Corporation of Delhi received numerous complaints of tree fall and waterlogging across the city. Traffic slowed on major roads, and waterlogging affected key points like Mahipalpur T-Point. The India Meteorological Department issued a red alert, forecasting more rain.

title: Hi’ locks a new release date as Kavin and Nayanthara’s fun promo confirms August 28
content: In an exciting update, the release date of Hi, starring Kavin alongside Nayanthara, has been postponed to August 28. This strategic move helps avoid a direct box office clash and grants extra time for marketing efforts. The film's creators revealed the new date in an engaging promotional video, with Vishnu Edavan at the helm, working alongside Nayanthara as a producer.

title: India's day out in Colombo: Gill sidelined by injury as bowlers find rhythm
content: India's bowlers gradually found their rhythm after a sluggish start as Manav Suthar, Ravindra Jadeja and Kuldeep Yadav picked up two wickets each to restrict SLC XI to 363 for 8 on the opening day of the warm-up match. Shubman Gill missed the day's play because of a finger injury, with KL Rahul leading the side.

title: US overtakes Gulf as India's biggest LPG supplier after Hormuz disruptions: Report
content: Supplies from Kuwait also fell sharply to 33,000 tonnes, down 43 per cent from June, while Qatar supplied just 19,000 tonnes. The contrast with the pre-conflict period has been striking. In January, the US exported only 268,000 tonnes of LPG to India, whereas the UAE supplied 826,000 tonnes. As a result, the US accounted for 73 per cent of India's LPG imports in July, compared with just 12 per cent in January.

title: 'Do not endorse anything said': MEA rejects Bangladesh's charge over Hasina event
content: Ministry of external affairs stated no government role in Sheikh Hasina's media event. The ministry does not endorse statements made at the private forum. Bangladesh expressed outrage over the interaction, calling it an affront to its sovereignty. Dhaka urged India to clarify its policy regarding conspiratorial activities. Both nations seek constructive relations based on mutual respect and equality.

title: Jantar Mantar 'terror plot' row: Amritsar top cop shunted; BJP cries foul
content: Amritsar Police Commissioner Gurpreet Singh Bhullar’s sudden removal has taken many by surprise. Harmanbir Singh Gill, who is currently the DIG of Border Range, has assumed the additional duty as CP. While the government cites administrative grounds for the change, rumors indicate that a controversial statement may have influenced this decision, leading to political debates about its timing.

title: Allahabad HC grants parole to Atiq Ahmed's jailed sons for Abaan Ahmed's burial
content: The Allahabad High Court granted parole to Atiq Ahmed's jailed sons, Umar and Ali. They will attend the burial of their younger brother, Abaan Ahmed, who died in an accident. Abaan Ahmed was killed along with his friend Sonu in a road accident in Jhansi. Their bodies were brought to Prayagraj for the funeral service. The court order came after a petition filed by Atiq Ahmed's sister.

title: Jai Moondra: Rajasthan boy who found international cricket in Ireland
content: Jai Moondra left Tonk for higher studies in Ireland, believing cricket was behind him. But while chasing coding deadlines in Dublin, the dream stayed alive at Leinster Cricket Club. After impressing in his maiden T20I series against India and making his ODI debut, the fast bowler's remarkable journey traces back to Rajasthan, a Pakistani mentor in Dublin, an Indian coach in Jaipur, and years of quiet perseverance.

title: Patna erupts after fatal bus accident; mob torches vehicles, storms police post
content: Tragedy struck in Patna's Chhoti Pahadi when a pedestrian lost their life due to a bus collision on NH-30. The community erupted in fury, setting the bus and multiple police vehicles ablaze in retaliation. In the chaos, motorcycles were vandalized and a police post was attacked, leading to assaults on journalists capturing the unrest. Police had to step in to restore order amidst the turmoil.

title: 'He was my sponsor': How Virat Kohli helped CWG gold medallist Sakshi Chaudhary
content: Sakshi Chaudhary proudly claimed gold at the 2026 Commonwealth Games, attributing much of her success to the invaluable support from Virat Kohli's foundation. Making a strategic move to a lighter weight category turned out to be a winning decision. This endeavor led India to an impressive 2026 boxing tally of ten medals, including seven shining golds, marking a triumphant milestone for the nation's athletic representation.

title: Dipa Karmakar's journey from flat feet to making history in gymnastics
content: Dipa Karmakar made history as India's first female gymnast to compete in the Olympics, overcoming significant challenges like flat feet and a lack of resources. She shined at the 2016 Rio Games with an impressive vault that garnered national acclaim. Following her success, she claimed gold at an international event and received many prestigious accolades. Despite facing injuries, Karmakar showed remarkable resilience, returning to gymnastics time and again.

title: 'Feared social stigma': Delhi man drowns pregnant teen daughter in Chambal
content: In a tragic turn of events, a pregnant teenager was reportedly drowned in the Chambal river by her own father and brother-in-law. The young girl, who was four months pregnant, was allegedly coerced into jumping into the river. When she resisted, they overpowered her, leading to her death. The father admitted to the crime, driven by the fear of societal judgment, while the brother-in-law has also been taken into custody.

title: Scientists discover Titan's methane rainstorms are more intense than expected
content: On the distant moon Titan, intense methane rainstorms transform the icy terrain, creating striking alluvial fans that showcase the areas most affected by these rare deluges. Scientists leverage data from the Cassini mission to create models of these phenomena, which happen less frequently than once every Titan year—a period nearly equivalent to 30 Earth years. Understanding Titan's unique weather patterns offers insights into extreme rainfall events here on our planet.

title: Why stock market's close is now an auction - explained
content: For over three decades, the closing price was the volume-weighted average (VWAP) of all trades between 3:00 pm and 3:30 pm. Nobody actually traded at that price. It was a calculation, not a transaction. For long-term investors, nothing changes. For index funds and traders, the closing routine is now different.

title: 'Paper Agreement With Turkey, Pak Will Not Bring You Security': Iran To Saudi
content: Ebrahim Rezaei, a member of Iran's Parliament and National Security and Foreign Policy Commission, wrote, "Saudis must know that a paper agreement with Turkey and Pakistan will not bring them security, just as years of one-sided nursing to the Americans did not bring them security."

content: The proposed law will pave the way for private universities in Delhi, with a 25% quota for Delhi students and provisions for strict government oversight.

content: Apart from waterlogging, traffic congestion was reported from several major places across Delhi, including Mehrauli-Badarpur Road, ITO, Wazirabad Road.

title: 'Even When He Sleeps, He Sees Sena Corporator': Lawyer Of Assaulted Doctor
content: The court ordered Ramesh Mhatre to stay outside Maharashtra while the trial continues. Instead, the court directed him to stay at Nazri Resort & Lawns, a four-star resort in Goa.

content: India has also increased domestic LPG production to offset lower imports from Gulf suppliers, Union Oil Minister Hardeep Singh Puri said

content: Shashi Tharoor said the Congress had taken up similar concerns months before they became the centrepiece of the CJP's agitation.

content: The forum's spokesperson Ellen Brooks said the proposed provisions could affect funds to schools, hospitals and charitable organisations that provide services to poor and disadvantaged communities.

title: Faction Wars: How Internal Rifts Are Shaping Punjab's Polls
content: With the 2027 assembly elections drawing closer, Punjab's political parties face a common challenge: containing dissidence, uniting their factions and holding together for the campaign ahead.

title: Lok Sabha Passes Bill Granting Tax Exemption To Foreign Bond Investors
content: The Bill provides the exemption to Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) investing in government securities (G-Secs), covering interest earned on such securities as well as capital gains arising from their sale, exchange or transfer.

content: Meta, owned by Mark Zuckerberg, has been instructed to include more people who understand Indian languages and context in their teams, sources said

title: ChatGPT, Button Cameras, Earbuds: How Fireman Ran High-Tech Cheating Racket
content: The case came to light on May 26 after two candidates were caught cheating during a recruitment examination conducted by the Central Sanskrit University in Delhi.

content: Although the government has managed to pass several important bills, attention is now focused on two specific ones: the Constitution Amendment Bill regarding delimitation and women's reservation, and the FCRA Amendment Bill concerning foreign contributions

content: First conceptualised in 2002, the highway project is rooted in India's Act East policy to boost regional trade, tourism, and further economic activity through connectivity and integration with ASEAN.

content: The Malwa belt is dominated by the Jat Sikh landlord community, which makes up 35 to 40 per cent of the electorate.

content: Experts urge digital literacy and healthy online habits over outright bans, highlighting social media's role in children's career growth and emotional development.
